blocks.text: The opening places Israel in the wilderness of Sinai, with Egypt remembered as the land already left behind. Sinai is the starting point of Numbers rather than its destination; the book’s movement will eventually carry the people toward the plains of Moab.

sections.title: The Census in the Book’s Larger Design

blocks.text: This census does more than supply a total at Sinai. Together with the later census in Numbers 26, it frames the book’s transition from the generation counted at Sinai to the generation prepared for inheritance near Moab. The long tribal count therefore belongs to the larger movement of Numbers from preparation at Sinai, through the wilderness journey, to renewed preparation on the plains of Moab.

sections.title: How Should the Numbers Be Understood?

blocks.text: The census concludes with 603,550 men aged twenty and above who were able to go to war, excluding the Levites. The scale of this wilderness population, as well as its relationship to the later census, has received differing literary and historical interpretations. Because the available context does not settle among those reconstructions, the size and character of the totals should be treated as a genuine interpretive question rather than explained with unwarranted certainty.
